claims.text: The bond-coat feedstock is an FeCoNiCrAl high-entropy alloy with a particle size of 15–45 μm.
Conventional thermal-spray methods produce less than the required coating thickness from the 15–45 μm feedstock.
ID-HVAF spraying with a propylene-fueled i7 torch provides a lower-temperature deposition environment than the baseline process.
Using the proposed ID-HVAF process will enhance in-flight particle dynamics.
The lower operational temperature will reduce oxidation during spraying.
The lower-temperature ID-HVAF environment will improve particle flattening upon impact.
The proposed process will improve bonding between deposited particles and the substrate or previously deposited material.
Improved particle flattening and bonding will increase deposition efficiency.
Increased deposition efficiency will produce a thicker FeCoNiCrAl bond coat from the 15–45 μm feedstock.
The proposed process will produce a statistically significant increase in as-sprayed coating thickness relative to higher-temperature conventional spraying.
The thicker coating will retain sound microstructural integrity.
The thicker coating will maintain minimal as-sprayed oxidation.
The predicted benefit should remain effective under feedstock and service conditions similar to those used in thermal barrier coating systems.
Applicability to other alloy compositions or drastically different service environments has not been established.
The magnitude of the expected thickness increase has not been quantified.
